\chapter{Chapter05 — Krawtchouk Polynomials}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from FABL.Chapter05.KrawtchoukPolynomials
\section{Overview}

Declarations of the Lean module \texttt{FABL.Chapter05.KrawtchoukPolynomials}.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{definition}[Number of negative coordinates]
\lean{FABL.negativeCoordinateCount}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b005}
\label{FABL.negativeCoordinateCount}
\leanok
For a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$, its negative-coordinate count is the number of
indices $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$ for which $x_i=-1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Krawtchouk value on the cube]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukValue}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b005}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.monomial}
For a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ and a natural number $j$, its Krawtchouk value is the
sum of the degree-$j$ cube monomials evaluated at $x$, over all subsets of
$\{1,\ldots,n\}$ of size $j$.
\end{definition}

\begin{definition}[Krawtchouk generating polynomial]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b006
}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.signValue}
For a sign vector $x\in\{-1,1\}^{n}$, define its Krawtchouk generating polynomial by
$K_x(X)=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\bigl(1+\sigma(x_i)X\bigr)\in\mathbb{R}[X]$, where $\sigma(1)=1$
and $\sigma(-1)=-1$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{4}
For a positive integer $n$, let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ and let $j\ge 0$. The coefficient of
$t^j$ in $\prod_{i=1}^n(1+x_i t)$ equals
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\},\,|S|=j}\prod_{i\in S}x_i$.
\end{theorem}

  {FABL.krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial}
  {context}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b005,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b009}
\proofstep
  {FABL.krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial_eq_subset_sum}
  {context}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b009}
\difficulty{3}
Let $x$ be a sign assignment on $n$ coordinates and let $\rho\in\mathbb{R}$. The
polynomial $\prod_{i=1}^n(1+x_iX)$, evaluated at $\rho$, equals
$\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\bigl(\prod_{i\in S}x_i\bigr)\rho^{|S|}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Generating sum for Krawtchouk values]
\lean{FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue_mul_pow}
\label{FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue_mul_pow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.krawtchoukValue, FABL.monomial}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$, and $\rho\in\mathbb R$. For
each $j$, sum $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ over all $j$-element subsets
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$; the sum of these values weighted by $\rho^j$, for
$j=0,\ldots,n$, equals $\sum_{S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}}\left(\prod_{i\in
S}x_i\right)\rho^{|S|}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of sign monomials]
\lean{FABL.sum_monomial_eq_point_indicator}
\label{FABL.sum_monomial_eq_point_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.eval_krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial, FABL.indicatorPolynomial, FABL.krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial, FABL.monomial, FABL.signValue, FABL.signValue_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The sum over all subsets
$S\subseteq[n]$ of the monomial $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ equals $2^n\prod_{i=1}^n(1+x_i)/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Sum of Krawtchouk values]
\lean{FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue}
\label{FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.indicatorPolynomial, FABL.krawtchoukValue, FABL.monomial, FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue_mul_pow, FABL.sum_monomial_eq_point_indicator}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $x\in\{\pm1\}^n$. For each $j$, sum the
monomials $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ over all $j$-element subsets
$S\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, and then sum these values over $j=0,\ldots,n$. The
result is $2^n\prod_{i=0}^{n-1}(1+x_i)/2$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of a finite sum]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_finset_sum}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_finset_sum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.pmfExpectation}
\difficulty{3}
Let $\Omega$ be a finite set, let $p$ be a probability mass function on $\Omega$, let
$s$ be a finite set of indices, and let $f_i:\Omega\to\mathbb{R}$ for each index $i$.
The expectation under $p$ of the sum over $i\in s$ of $f_i$ equals the sum over $i\in s$
of their expectations under $p$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Expectation of a point indicator]
\lean{FABL.pmfExpectation_point_indicator}
\label{FABL.pmfExpectation_point_indicator}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.indicatorPolynomial, FABL.indicatorPolynomial_eq_ite, FABL.pmfExpectation}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $p$ be a probability mass function on the sign cube
$\{-1,1\}^n$, and let $a\in\{-1,1\}^n$. The expectation under $p$ of the function that
equals $1$ at $a$ and $0$ at every other point is the probability mass $p(a)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Krawtchouk generating identity]
\lean{FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue_mul_pow_eq_noiseKernel}
\label{FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue_mul_pow_eq_noiseKernel}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.indicatorPolynomial, FABL.krawtchoukValue, FABL.monomial, FABL.noiseKernel, FABL.pmfExpectation, FABL.pmfExpectation_const_mul, FABL.pmfExpectation_finset_sum, FABL.pmfExpectation_noiseKernel_monomial, FABL.pmfExpectation_point_indicator, FABL.sum_krawtchoukValue_mul_pow, FABL.sum_monomial_eq_point_indicator}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $x\in\{-1,1\}^n$. For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$,
the sum of the degree-$j$ Krawtchouk values at $x$, weighted by $\rho^j$ for $0\le j\le
n$, equals $2^n$ times the probability that independently flipping each coordinate of
$x$ with correlation parameter $\rho$ produces the all-ones vector.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Power of a negative indeterminate]
\lean{FABL.neg_X_pow_eq}
\label{FABL.neg_X_pow_eq}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $m$, the polynomial $(-X)^m$ over $\mathbb R$ equals $(-1)^m
X^m$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficients of a signed monomial power]
\lean{FABL.coeff_neg_X_pow}
\label{FABL.coeff_neg_X_pow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.neg_X_pow_eq}
\difficulty{1}
For nonnegative integers $m$ and $k$, the coefficient of $t^k$ in $(-t)^m$ is $(-1)^m$
if $k=m$, and is $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Coefficients of a binomial power]
\lean{FABL.coeff_one_sub_X_pow}
\label{FABL.coeff_one_sub_X_pow}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.coeff_neg_X_pow}
\difficulty{5}
For nonnegative integers $z$ and $k$, the coefficient of $t^k$ in $(1-t)^z$ is
$(-1)^k\binom{z}{k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Krawtchouk polynomial]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b006
}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial}
\leanok
For natural numbers $n$ and $j$, define a polynomial in $\mathbb{R}[X]$ by summing over
$0\le k\le j$ the terms
\[(-1)^k\frac{(n)_{\underline{k}}}{k!}\,\frac{(n-X)_{\underline{j-k}}}{(j-k)!},\]
where $(y)_{\underline{m}}=y(y-1)\cdots(y-m+1)$ is the falling factorial and
$(y)_{\underline{0}}=1$.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a complemented linear polynomial]
\lean{FABL.complementLinear_natDegree}
\label{FABL.complementLinear_natDegree}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the polynomial $n-X$ has natural degree $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leading coefficient of a complemented linear polynomial]
\lean{FABL.complementLinear_leadingCoeff}
\label{FABL.complementLinear_leadingCoeff}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$, the polynomial $n-X$ has leading coefficient $-1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a normalized falling factorial]
\lean{FABL.chooseFactor_natDegree}
\label{FABL.chooseFactor_natDegree}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $k$, the polynomial $\frac{1}{k!}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(X-j)$ has
natural degree $k$, where the empty product is $1$ when $k=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leading coefficient of a normalized falling factorial]
\lean{FABL.chooseFactor_leadingCoeff}
\label{FABL.chooseFactor_leadingCoeff}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $k$, let $(X)_k=\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(X-j)$ be the falling-factorial polynomial. The leading coefficient of
$\frac{1}{k!}(X)_{k}$ is $\frac{1}{k!}$, with the empty product interpreted as $1$ when
$k=0$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a complemented falling factorial]
\lean{FABL.complementChooseFactor_natDegree}
\label{FABL.complementChooseFactor_natDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.complementLinear_natDegree}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, the real polynomial in the indeterminate $X$ given by
$\frac{1}{k!}\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}(n-X-j)$ has degree $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leading coefficient of a complemented falling factorial]
\lean{FABL.complementChooseFactor_leadingCoeff}
\label{FABL.complementChooseFactor_leadingCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.complementLinear_leadingCoeff, FABL.complementLinear_natDegree}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n$ and $k$, let $Q_{n,k}(X)=\prod_{i=0}^{k-1}(n-X-i)$. The leading
coefficient of $Q_{n,k}(X)/k!$ is $(-1)^k/k!$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a Krawtchouk summand]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukSummand_natDegree}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukSummand_natDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.chooseFactor_leadingCoeff, FABL.chooseFactor_natDegree, FABL.complementChooseFactor_leadingCoeff, FABL.complementChooseFactor_natDegree}
\difficulty{4}
For natural numbers $n,j,k$ with $k\le j$, the natural degree of the $k$th summand in
the defining sum for the Krawtchouk polynomial of parameters $n,j$ is $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leading coefficient of a Krawtchouk summand]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukSummand_leadingCoeff}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukSummand_leadingCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.chooseFactor_leadingCoeff, FABL.complementChooseFactor_leadingCoeff}
\difficulty{3}
For all natural numbers $n,j,k$, the leading coefficient of the $k$th summand in the
defining sum for the Krawtchouk polynomial of parameters $n,j$ is
$(-1)^k(k!)^{-1}((j-k)!)^{-1}(-1)^{j-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Factorial inverse identity]
\lean{FABL.factorial_inverse_identity}
\label{FABL.factorial_inverse_identity}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $j$ and $k$ with $k \le j$, the product of the reciprocals of $k!$
and $(j-k)!$ equals $\binom{j}{k}$ times the reciprocal of $j!$:
$\frac{1}{k!}\frac{1}{(j-k)!}=\binom{j}{k}\frac{1}{j!}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Signed factorial inverse identity]
\lean{FABL.signed_factorial_inverse_identity}
\label{FABL.signed_factorial_inverse_identity}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.factorial_inverse_identity}
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $j$ and $k$ with $k\le j$, the following identity holds over the
real numbers:
$$(-1)^k\frac{1}{k!}\frac{1}{(j-k)!}(-1)^{j-k}=(-1)^j\binom{j}{k}\frac{1}{j!}.$$
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Leading coefficient of a Krawtchouk sum]
\lean{FABL.sum_krawtchoukSummand_leadingCoeff}
\label{FABL.sum_krawtchoukSummand_leadingCoeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.krawtchoukSummand_leadingCoeff, FABL.signed_factorial_inverse_identity}
\difficulty{4}
For nonnegative integers $n,j$, let $(t)_r=\prod_{s=0}^{r-1}(t-s)$ denote the falling
factorial polynomial, with $(t)_0=1$. The sum, for $k=0,\ldots,j$, of the leading
coefficients of the polynomials $\frac{(-1)^k}{k!}(t)_k\,\frac{1}{(j-k)!}(n-t)_{j-k}$
is $(-1)^j2^j/j!$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Degree of a Krawtchouk polynomial]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial_natDegree}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial_natDegree}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial, FABL.krawtchoukSummand_natDegree, FABL.sum_krawtchoukSummand_leadingCoeff}
\difficulty{5}
For natural numbers $n$ and $j$ with $j\le n$, the natural degree of the Krawtchouk
polynomial $K_{n,j}$ is $j$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Binomial coefficient polynomial evaluation]
\lean{FABL.eval_chooseFactorPolynomial}
\label{FABL.eval_chooseFactorPolynomial}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
For natural numbers $z$ and $k$, evaluating the polynomial
$(k!)^{-1}(X(X-1)	imes	ext{etc.}	imes(X-k+1))$ at $z$ gives the binomial coefficient:
its value is $\binom{z}{k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Complementary binomial coefficient evaluation]
\lean{FABL.eval_complementChooseFactorPolynomial}
\label{FABL.eval_complementChooseFactorPolynomial}
\leanok
\difficulty{3}
Let $n,z,k$ be natural numbers with $z\le n$. Evaluating the polynomial
$(k!)^{-1}(X(X-1)\times\text{etc.}\times(X-k+1))$ after substituting $n-X$ for $X$, at
$z$, gives $\binom{n-z}{k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Signed Binomial Sum for Krawtchouk Values]
\lean{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_signedChooseSum}
\label{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_signedChooseSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.eval_chooseFactorPolynomial, FABL.eval_complementChooseFactorPolynomial, FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n,z,j$ be nonnegative integers with $z\le n$, and let $K_{n,j}$ be the Krawtchouk
polynomial. Then $K_{n,j}(z)=\sum_{k=0}^{j}(-1)^k\binom{z}{k}\binom{n-z}{j-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Signed binomial coefficient formula]
\lean{FABL.coeff_countGeneratingPolynomial_eq_signedChooseSum}
\label{FABL.coeff_countGeneratingPolynomial_eq_signedChooseSum}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.coeff_one_sub_X_pow}
\difficulty{4}
For all nonnegative integers $n,z,j$, the coefficient of $X^j$ in $(1-X)^z(1+X)^{n-z}$
over $\mathbb R$ is $\sum_{k=0}^{j}(-1)^k\binom{z}{k}\binom{n-z}{j-k}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Krawtchouk Polynomial Evaluation]
\lean{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_coeff}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b009}
\label{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_coeff}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.coeff_countGeneratingPolynomial_eq_signedChooseSum, FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_signedChooseSum, FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial}
\proofstep

\difficulty{1}
Let $n,z,j$ be nonnegative integers with $z\le n$, and let $K_{n,j}$ be the Krawtchouk
polynomial. Its value at $z$ is the coefficient of $X^j$ in $(1-X)^z(1+X)^{n-z}$:
$K_{n,j}(z)=[X^j](1-X)^z(1+X)^{n-z}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Krawtchouk Polynomial and Generating Coefficient]
\lean{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_coeff_countGenerating}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p137-b009}
\label{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_coeff_countGenerating}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.eval_krawtchoukPolynomial_eq_coeff, FABL.krawtchoukPolynomial}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n,z,j$ be nonnegative integers with $z\le n$, and let $K_{n,j}$ be the Krawtchouk
polynomial. Then $K_{n,j}(z)$ equals the coefficient of $X^j$ in $(1-X)^z(1+X)^{n-z}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Bound on negative coordinates]
\lean{FABL.negativeCoordinateCount_le}
\label{FABL.negativeCoordinateCount_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.negativeCoordinateCount}
\difficulty{3}
For every point $x$ of the $n$-dimensional sign cube, the number of coordinates of $x$
equal to $-1$ is at most $n$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Krawtchouk value as a polynomial coefficient]
\lean{FABL.krawtchoukValue_eq_coeff_negativeCount}
\label{FABL.krawtchoukValue_eq_coeff_negativeCount}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.coeff_krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial, FABL.krawtchoukGeneratingPolynomial_eq_negativeCount, FABL.krawtchoukValue, FABL.negativeCoordinateCount}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $x\in\{−1,1\}^n$, and let $j$ be a natural number. The
sum of the degree-$j$ monomials in the coordinates of $x$ equals the coefficient of
$X^j$ in $(1-X)^{m}(1+X)^{n-m}$, where $m$ is the number of negative coordinates of $x$.
\end{theorem}
